name: Deterministic Integer 3SUM in O(n^1.999017): Sharp Binomial-Tail Analysis
description:
## Why sharpen the integer 3SUM exponent?

**3SUM** asks whether an input sequence contains three entries at different positions whose sum is zero. The classical quadratic running time makes it a benchmark for fine-grained algorithm design: even a small fixed improvement in the exponent changes its asymptotic complexity. The setting here is polynomially bounded integers and a deterministic word RAM; the input-size exponent, rather than an experimental speedup, is the quantity being studied.

[Alman and Vassilevska Williams (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06783v1) give a deterministic truly subquadratic integer 3SUM algorithm through thin matrix products and reductions involving Exact Triangle. [Xu's manuscript, *Deterministic Integer 3SUM in O(n^1.999017) Time via a Sharper Binomial-Tail Analysis*](https://hexagonmath.org/submit/d57cba23-2d89-4bcb-8180-7c1bde7d14e3), dated 13 October 2026, refines the analysis of that framework. Its claimed bound is the formalization target here. The Hexagon link identifies the author's submission page, which may require authentication; it is not presented as a public article identifier or evidence of peer review.

## Inputs, machine model, and analytic quantities

An input of size $n$ is a function $x:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb Z$. For a fixed natural number $\kappa$, every entry obeys $|x_i|\le n^\kappa$. Acceptance means that there are pairwise distinct indices $i,j,k$ with $x_i+x_j+x_k=0$. Repeated values at different positions are allowed. This is a decision problem, so the algorithm need not return a witness triple.

The **word-RAM specification** is the campaign's existing `EndStatement` definition, imported from its [foundation mission](https://prove2.me/missions/487064c8-0ffb-4779-802b-6824b289a73c). For each fixed $\kappa$, one finite deterministic program, one word-width threshold constant, and one time-bound function must work for all input sizes and all word widths above that threshold. Words have finite signed interpretations; arithmetic, indirect memory access, branching, acceptance, and rejection are defined operationally. The result concerns this exact model.

For the supporting analysis, let $H(u)=-u\log u-(1-u)\log(1-u)$, with endpoint values $H(0)=H(1)=0$. All logarithms are natural. For an integer $c>10$, a positive integer $m$, and $0<\theta<0.9$, set $L=cm$, $D=4^m$, $t=\lceil\theta m\rceil$, and

$$\beta_d=\binom L{m-d}9^{L-m+d},\qquad M=\beta_0.$$

The **sharp preprocessing saving**, **query exponent**, and **encoding exponent** are

$$\gamma_*(c,\theta)=\frac{cH(1/c)-cH((1-\theta)/c)-\theta\log9}{\log4},$$
$$q(\theta)=\frac{H(\theta)+\theta\log9}{\log4},\qquad A(c)=\frac{c\log10-cH(1/c)/2-(c-1)\log3}{\log4}.$$

These auxiliary definitions describe costs; they neither redefine 3SUM nor assume the existence of a fast algorithm.

## Formalization targets

The campaign goal is the exact fixed bound

$$\texttt{EndStatement.ThreeSum.SolvedInTime}\;1.999017.$$

The first supporting milestone is the two-sided binomial entropy estimate. The second is the manuscript's normalized tail bound

$$\frac1M\sum_{d=t}^m\beta_d\le\frac{cm+1}{1-9/(c-1)}D^{-\gamma_*(c,\theta)}.$$

A further milestone establishes strict improvement over the earlier preprocessing saving $\gamma(c,\theta)=\theta\log((c-1)/9)/\log4$ at fixed parameters. The algorithmic milestone combines the manuscript's Propositions 4.1 and 5.1: admissible sharp-tail parameters must yield a program satisfying the shared 3SUM specification, not merely a numerical inequality.

The final supporting milestone certifies the exact choice

$$c=21,\qquad\theta=0.11202,\qquad a=0.05665,\qquad s=0.06945.$$

It includes the preprocessing, query, encoding, prime-selection, and instance-construction inequalities, together with

$$2-as/4=1.999016414375,\qquad1.999017-(2-as/4)=0.000000585625>0.$$

Every terminating decimal denotes an exact rational number. The target is the fixed big-$O$ exponent 1.999017; the smaller cutoff is accompanied by residual asymptotic losses in the manuscript and is not asserted as the same fixed bound.

## What completing this mission would establish

A complete proof would certify the manuscript's improved integer 3SUM bound in the campaign's common machine model. The gain is an analysis refinement of the inherited algorithm and reductions. It does not claim a new algorithmic framework, optimal parameters, global optimality, or priority over all other work.

The manuscript also gives an auxiliary $O(n^{1.999073})$ bound by retuning the previous estimate. That weaker result is background, not this mission's campaign value. The existing upstream formalization is prior work; it does not automatically certify either refinement. The supplied rational interval verifier checks the parameter inequalities, but those checks alone do not prove a word-RAM running-time theorem. The main goal and the newly drafted supporting statements remain open Lean proof obligations.

## Where the difficulty lies

A better tail estimate is insufficient unless every other cost remains within the final budget. Shared encoding work, all queries, deterministic prime selection, witness scanning, and instance construction must be included. The word-size and address bounds must remain valid after changing parameters. Ceiling operations, restricting $D$ to powers of four, and bounded-size exceptions must also be handled.

The central formalization burden is the connection between the analytic estimates and an actual deterministic program. Assuming an oracle with the desired running time would remove that burden and would not establish the stated target. Likewise, checking a finite range of sizes or a floating-point optimizer's output cannot establish the universal algorithmic statement.

## Formalization scope and conventions

The environment is Lean 4.33.1 with Mathlib revision `0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474`. The foundation reference and the campaign goal's import are retained. Supporting definitions use real logarithms, real powers, natural binomial coefficients, finite sums, and a natural ceiling. Domain hypotheses exclude invalid entropy-tail regimes; endpoint binomial cases are included explicitly.

For $r=1999017/1000000$, the shared time predicate means that there exists $K\in\mathbb N$ such that $T(n)^{1000000}\le K n^{1999017}$ for every $n\ge2$. Correctness and termination still cover every input size, including $n<3$. The manuscript's $\kappa\ge1$ convention must be extended to the campaign's $\kappa=0$ case, and its word-size analysis must justify uniform correctness at every sufficiently large word width. Both are explicit interface obligations.

Reusable contributions include entropy and tail estimates, rigorous logarithm enclosures, and parameterized cost-to-program results. Existing compatible library results should be reused where available. The manuscript and metadata were prepared with AI assistance; this mission makes no claim of completed human review or completed formal verification of the improved bound.

## Selected references

- Yuxuan Xu, *Deterministic Integer 3SUM in O(n^1.999017) Time via a Sharper Binomial-Tail Analysis*, manuscript, 13 October 2026. [Author-supplied Hexagon submission page](https://hexagonmath.org/submit/d57cba23-2d89-4bcb-8180-7c1bde7d14e3). Target: Theorem 1.1; supporting analysis: Sections 3–6.
- Josh Alman and Virginia Vassilevska Williams, *Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs*, arXiv preprint, 2026. [arXiv:2610.06783v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06783v1). Inherited ingredients: Section 4, Lemma 29, Theorem 30, Corollary 31, and the deterministic reductions cited in Xu's Section 2.
- Anthropic, *Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP: a Lean 4 formalization*, source repository, 2026. [Pinned source at commit e1a4e6508154ea59f030480661590a9fe3018011](https://github.com/anthropics/formal-math/tree/e1a4e6508154ea59f030480661590a9fe3018011/3sum-apsp). Its `EndStatement.lean` supplies the shared specification, not a proof of this mission's new exponent.

items.natural_language_statement:
Defines the concrete deterministic word RAM and the problem specifications used by the source formalization of truly subcubic APSP. The machine has signed finite-width words, arithmetic and memory instructions, conditional jumps, and accept/reject verdicts. Its input convention and step-count predicate specify what it means for one program to solve a problem uniformly over input sizes and sufficiently large logarithmic word widths.

The problem interfaces include Exact Triangle, min-plus matrix multiplication, and all-pairs shortest paths. APSP instances have no negative-weight closed walks; outputs encode reachability and attained minimum distances. The source's rational-power running-time predicate represents $O(n^r)$ using an integer inequality.

These declarations provide the original `EndStatement` namespace used by the checked algorithm proofs. They are specifications, with no assumed algorithm-correctness or running-time theorems.

References:

1. Josh Alman and Virginia Vassilevska Williams, *Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs*, source formalization, `EndStatement.lean`.

module

/-! Claims of the paper «Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs» (Josh
Alman, Virginia Vassilevska Williams), about programs of a word RAM defined here. Imports nothing, proves nothing. -/

@[expose] public section

namespace EndStatement

/-- `i j k` name cells, `l` a position in the program, `[i]` is the word in cell `i`. The only constant is 1. -/
inductive Instr where
  | one (i : Int)             -- [i] := 1
  | add (i j k : Int)         -- [i] := [j] + [k]
  | sub (i j k : Int)         -- [i] := [j] - [k]
  | mul (i j k : Int)         -- [i] := [j] * [k]
  | load (i j : Int)          -- [i] := [[j]]
  | store (i j : Int)         -- [[i]] := [j]
  | bltz (i : Int) (l : Nat)  -- if [i] < 0, go to position l
  | accept
  | reject

/-- The verdict and the final memory, if `P`, run from position `pc` on memory `m`, halts within `t` steps, the halting
step counted; past its end `P` rejects. Addresses are read signed; `bltz` jumps on a negative word; `write` runs on. -/
def exec {W : Nat} (P : List Instr) : (t pc : Nat) → (m : Int → BitVec W) → Option (Bool × (Int → BitVec W))
  | 0, _, _ => none
  | t + 1, pc, m =>
    let write (i : Int) (v : BitVec W) := exec P t (pc + 1) fun x => if x = i then v else m x
    match P.getD pc .reject with
    | .one i => write i 1
    | .add i j k => write i (m j + m k)
    | .sub i j k => write i (m j - m k)
    | .mul i j k => write i (m j * m k)
    | .load i j => write i (m (m j).toInt)
    | .store i j => write (m i).toInt (m j)
    | .bltz i l => exec P t (if (m i).toInt < 0 then l else pc + 1) m
    | .accept => some (true, m)
    | .reject => some (false, m)

/-- The memory at the start: `ws` in cells 0, 1, 2, …, and 0 in every other cell. -/
def loadWords (W : Nat) (ws : List Int) : Int → BitVec W :=
  fun a => if a < 0 then 0 else BitVec.ofInt W (ws.getD a.toNat 0)

/-- `T(n) = O(n^r)`, both sides raised to the power `r.den`: core Lean has no fractional powers. For `r = 1.9992 =
2499/1250` it says `T(n)^1250 ≤ K n^2499`. -/
def BigO (T : Nat → Nat) (r : Rat) : Prop :=
  ∃ K : Nat, ∀ n ≥ 2, T n ^ r.den ≤ K * n ^ r.num.toNat

/-- `yes`: when to accept (always, if not given). `output`: a condition on the cells after the input, read as signed. -/
structure Problem where
  Instance : Nat → Type
  input {n : Nat} : Instance n → List Int
  yes {n : Nat} : Instance n → Prop := fun _ => True
  output {n : Nat} : Instance n → (Nat → Int) → Prop := fun _ _ => True

/-- One run: with `n` in cell 0 and the input after it, `P` halts within `t` steps with the right verdict and output. -/
def Problem.SolvedBy (Q : Problem) {n : Nat} (x : Q.Instance n) (P : List Instr) (W t : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ verdict m, exec P t 0 (loadWords W ((n : Int) :: Q.input x)) = some (verdict, m) ∧
    (verdict = true ↔ Q.yes x) ∧ Q.output x fun a => (m (1 + (Q.input x).length + a : Nat)).toInt

/-- Theorem 2: «a word RAM with O(log n)-bit words», «all numbers in the input are integers of absolute value
n^O(1)»: for every `κ`, one `P`, `b`, `T` for all instances, correct at every `W ≥ b(⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1)`. -/
def Problem.SolvedInTime (Q : Problem) (r : Rat) : Prop :=
  ∀ κ : Nat, ∃ (P : List Instr) (b : Nat) (T : Nat → Nat), BigO T r ∧
    ∀ (n : Nat) (x : Q.Instance n), (∀ a ∈ Q.input x, a.natAbs ≤ n ^ κ) → ∀ W ≥ b * (Nat.log2 n + 1),
      Q.SolvedBy x P W (T n)

def rowByRow {n : Nat} (w : Fin n → Fin n → Int) : List Int :=
  (List.ofFn fun u => List.ofFn fun v => w u v).flatten

/-- Section 3.2: «S(a, b, c) := w(a, b) + w(b, c) + w(a, c). A zero triangle is a triangle … with S(a, b, c) = 0». -/
def ExactTriangle : Problem where
  Instance n := (Fin n → Fin n → Int) × (Fin n → Fin n → Int) × (Fin n → Fin n → Int)
  input := fun (wAB, wBC, wAC) => rowByRow wAB ++ rowByRow wBC ++ rowByRow wAC
  yes := fun (wAB, wBC, wAC) => ∃ a b c, wAB a b + wBC b c + wAC a c = 0

/-- Theorem 19: «ε_T := 0.0017». -/
def ε_T : Rat := 0.0017

/-- Theorem 19: «Exact Triangle … can be solved by a deterministic algorithm in … O(n^(3−ε_T)) time». -/
def Theorem_19 : Prop :=
  ExactTriangle.SolvedInTime (3 - ε_T)

/-- Section 1: «Given n numbers, decide whether three of them sum to 0». Three different positions. -/
def ThreeSum : Problem where
  Instance n := Fin n → Int
  input x := List.ofFn x
  yes x := ∃ i j k, i ≠ j ∧ j ≠ k ∧ i ≠ k ∧ x i + x j + x k = 0

/-- Theorem 22: «solve 3SUM on n integers of absolute value at most n^ν», in time «O(n^1.9992)». -/
def Theorem_22_3SUM : Prop :=
  ThreeSum.SolvedInTime 1.9992

/-- Output, row by row: entry `(i, j)` is the least of the sums `A i k + B k j`. -/
def MinPlusProduct : Problem where
  Instance n := (Fin n → Fin n → Int) × (Fin n → Fin n → Int)
  input := fun (A, B) => rowByRow A ++ rowByRow B
  output := fun {n} (A, B) out => ∀ i j : Fin n,
    (∃ k, out (i.val * n + j.val) = A i k + B k j) ∧ ∀ k, out (i.val * n + j.val) ≤ A i k + B k j

/-- Theorem 22: «the (min, +)-product of two n × n integer matrices», in time «O(n^2.99942)». -/
def Theorem_22_MinPlus : Prop :=
  MinPlusProduct.SolvedInTime 2.99942

/-- A path and its total weight; it may repeat vertices. -/
inductive Path {n : Nat} (w : Fin n → Fin n → Option Int) : Fin n → Fin n → Int → Prop
  | nil (i : Fin n) : Path w i i 0
  | cons {i j k : Fin n} {d e : Int} : w i j = some d → Path w j k e → Path w i k (d + e)

/-- Input: the 0/1 matrix of the edges, then the weights, with 0 for no edge. Output, two cells for each `(i, j)`: 1 if
there is a path, else 0; then the distance. -/
def APSP : Problem where
  Instance n := {w : Fin n → Fin n → Option Int // ∀ i d, Path w i i d → 0 ≤ d}
  input := fun ⟨w, _⟩ => rowByRow (fun i j => if (w i j).isSome then 1 else 0) ++ rowByRow fun i j => (w i j).getD 0
  output := fun {n} ⟨w, _⟩ out => ∀ i j : Fin n,
    let flag := out (2 * (i.val * n + j.val))
    let dist := out (2 * (i.val * n + j.val) + 1)
    (flag = 1 ∧ Path w i j dist ∧ ∀ e, Path w i j e → dist ≤ e) ∨ (flag = 0 ∧ ∀ e, ¬ Path w i j e)

/-- Theorem 22: «APSP on directed n-vertex graphs … and no negative cycles», in time «O(n^2.99942)». -/
def Theorem_22_APSP : Prop :=
  APSP.SolvedInTime 2.99942

/-- `w i j u v`: weight between `u` in part `i` and `v` in part `j`. All `k²` blocks are input; only `i < j` counts. -/
def ZeroWeightKClique (k : Nat) : Problem where
  Instance n := Fin k → Fin k → Fin n → Fin n → Int
  input w := (List.ofFn fun i => (List.ofFn fun j => rowByRow (w i j)).flatten).flatten
  yes {n} w := ∃ v : Fin k → Fin n,
    (List.ofFn fun j => (List.ofFn fun i => if i < j then w i j (v i) (v j) else 0).sum).sum = 0

/-- Corollary 39: «decide in O(n^(k−ε_T⌊k/3⌋)) time whether some k-clique … has total edge weight zero». -/
def Corollary_39_ZeroWeight : Prop :=
  ∀ k ≥ 3, (ZeroWeightKClique k).SolvedInTime (k - ε_T * (k / 3 : Nat))

end EndStatement

items.theorem_title: Entropy, box counts, and cost exponents for the sharp-tail analysis
items.natural_language_statement: Defines $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$ (so $H(0)=H(1)=0$), the old preprocessing saving $\gamma(c,\theta)=\theta\log((c-1)/9)/\log4$, the sharp saving $\gamma_*(c,\theta)=[cH(1/c)-cH((1-\theta)/c)-\theta\log9]/\log4$, the query exponent $q(\theta)=[H(\theta)+\theta\log9]/\log4$, and the encoding exponent $A(c)=[c\log10-cH(1/c)/2-(c-1)\log3]/\log4$. For natural numbers $c,m,d$, defines $\beta_d=\binom{cm}{m-d}9^{cm-m+d}$; later lemmas restrict to $c>10$, $m\ge1$ and $d\le m$. These are auxiliary analytic quantities, not a replacement for the campaign's shared word-RAM or 3SUM definitions. Real logarithms and division are total in Lean; intended domains are supplied by theorem hypotheses.
items.definition:
import Mathlib

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

namespace ThreeSumSharpTail

noncomputable def entropy (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  -x * Real.log x - (1 - x) * Real.log (1 - x)

noncomputable def oldSaving (c θ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  θ * Real.log ((c - 1) / 9) / Real.log 4

noncomputable def sharpSaving (c θ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (c * entropy (1 / c) - c * entropy ((1 - θ) / c) - θ * Real.log 9) / Real.log 4

noncomputable def queryExponent (θ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (entropy θ + θ * Real.log 9) / Real.log 4

noncomputable def encodingExponent (c : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (c * Real.log 10 - c * entropy (1 / c) / 2 - (c - 1) * Real.log 3) / Real.log 4

def boxCount (c m d : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.choose (c * m) (m - d) * 9 ^ (c * m - m + d)

end ThreeSumSharpTail
items.source: Yuxuan Xu, Deterministic Integer 3SUM in O(n^1.999017) Time via a Sharper Binomial-Tail Analysis (13 October 2026), Hexagon submission https://hexagonmath.org/submit/d57cba23-2d89-4bcb-8180-7c1bde7d14e3; Sections 2 and 3.
items.readback:
For every real number $x$, define $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$. Here and throughout these definitions, $\log$ is the total real logarithm: it is the natural logarithm on positive arguments, is $0$ at $0$, and equals $\log|x|$ on negative arguments. Thus $H$ is defined on all real numbers, not only $[0,1]$, and $H(0)=H(1)=0$.

For arbitrary real numbers $c$ and $\theta$, define $O(c,\theta)=\theta\log((c-1)/9)/\log4$. No restriction on either argument is imposed.

For arbitrary real numbers $c$ and $\theta$, define $S(c,\theta)=[cH(1/c)-cH((1-\theta)/c)-\theta\log9]/\log4$, where $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$. Real division is total, with division by $0$ equal to $0$, so this formula also defines $S(0,\theta)=-\theta\log9/\log4$.

For every real number $\theta$, define $Q(\theta)=[H(\theta)+\theta\log9]/\log4$, where $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$; there is no interval restriction on $\theta$.

For every real number $c$, define $E(c)=[c\log10-cH(1/c)/2-(c-1)\log3]/\log4$, where $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$ and division by zero is zero. In particular, $c=0$ is included and gives $E(0)=\log3/\log4$.

For all natural numbers $c,m,d$, including zero and without assuming $d\le m$ or $c\ge1$, define $B(c,m,d)=\binom{cm}{\max(m-d,0)}9^{\max(cm-m,0)+d}$. The subtractions inside the original natural-number expression are truncated at zero, and the exponent subtracts $m$ before adding $d$. The binomial coefficient is zero when its lower argument exceeds its upper argument. Consequently $B(c,0,d)=9^d$, and if $d>m$ the lower binomial argument is $0$, so $B(c,m,d)=9^{\max(cm-m,0)+d}$; these values are part of the definition even outside a tail range.

items.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSumSharpTail.binomial_entropy_bounds (r k : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hk : k ≤ r) :
    Real.exp ((r : ℝ) * ThreeSumSharpTail.entropy ((k : ℝ) / r)) / (r + 1) ≤ (Nat.choose r k : ℝ) ∧
    (Nat.choose r k : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp ((r : ℝ) * ThreeSumSharpTail.entropy ((k : ℝ) / r)) := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement: For integers $r\ge1$ and $0\le k\le r$, let $p=k/r$. Then $$\frac{e^{rH(p)}}{r+1}\le\binom rk\le e^{rH(p)}.$$ The endpoints $k=0,r$ are included. This is a standard estimate used by the manuscript, not a novelty claim.

theorem ThreeSumSharpTail.sharp_normalized_tail (c m : ℕ) (hc : 10 < c) (hm : 1 ≤ m)
    (θ : ℝ) (hθ0 : 0 < θ) (hθ9 : θ < 9 / 10) :
    ((∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc (⌈θ * (m : ℝ)⌉₊) m, ThreeSumSharpTail.boxCount c m d : ℕ) : ℝ) /
        (ThreeSumSharpTail.boxCount c m 0 : ℝ) ≤
      ((c : ℝ) * m + 1) / (1 - 9 / ((c : ℝ) - 1)) *
        Real.rpow ((4 : ℝ) ^ m) (-ThreeSumSharpTail.sharpSaving c θ) := by sorry

Then $$\frac1M\sum_{d=t}^{m}\beta_d\le\frac{cm+1}{1-9/(c-1)}D^{-\gamma_*(c,\theta)}.$$ The ceiling is part of the statement; $t=m$ is included.

items.readback: For every pair of natural numbers $c,m$ with $c>10$ and $m\ge1$, and every real $\theta$ with $0<\theta<9/10$, let $L=\lceil\theta m\rceil$; in this range the natural-number ceiling used in the statement is the ordinary ceiling and $1\le L\le m$. Define $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$, with the total real logarithm taking value $0$ at $0$ and the natural logarithm of the absolute value at a negative argument, and put $S=[cH(1/c)-cH((1-\theta)/c)-\theta\log9]/\log4$. Then $\displaystyle \frac{\sum_{d=L}^{m}\binom{cm}{m-d}9^{cm-m+d}}{\binom{cm}{m}9^{cm-m}}\le\frac{cm+1}{1-9/(c-1)}(4^m)^{-S}$. The sum includes both endpoints and is first formed as a natural number before being cast to the reals; every displayed division and the power with exponent $-S$ are real operations. The count used in the code is defined for arbitrary natural arguments by $\binom{cm}{\max(m-d,0)}9^{\max(cm-m,0)+d}$, but on the stated summation range no subtraction truncates. items.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSumSharpTail.admissible_parameters_solve_3sum
    (c : ℕ) (θ : ℝ) (a s r : ℚ) (hc : 10 < c)
    (hθ0 : 0 < θ) (hθ9 : θ < 9 / 10)
    (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hs0 : 0 < s) (hs1 : s < 1)
    (henc : (a : ℝ) * (ThreeSumSharpTail.encodingExponent c + ThreeSumSharpTail.sharpSaving c θ) < 1)
    (hprep : (s : ℝ) < ThreeSumSharpTail.sharpSaving c θ)
    (hquery : (s : ℝ) < 1 / 2 - ThreeSumSharpTail.queryExponent θ)
    (hprime : Real.log 7 / Real.log 2 + 3 * (a : ℝ) / 2 < 3 - (a : ℝ) * s / 2)
    (hbuild : 2 + (a : ℝ) * (1 + (s : ℝ) / 2) < 3 - (a : ℝ) * s / 2)
    (hr : 2 - a * s / 4 < r) :
    EndStatement.ThreeSum.SolvedInTime r := by sorry
items.natural_language_statement:
Let $c>10$ be an integer, $0<\theta<0.9$, and let $a,s,r$ be rational with $0<a<1$ and $0<s<1$. Suppose
$$a(A(c)+\gamma_*(c,\theta))<1,\qquad s<\gamma_*(c,\theta),\qquad s<\tfrac12-q(\theta),$$
$$\log_2 7+\tfrac32a<3-as/2,\qquad 2+a(1+s/2)<3-as/2,\qquad r>2-as/4.$$
Then deterministic integer 3SUM satisfies the campaign's exact shared predicate `EndStatement.ThreeSum.SolvedInTime r`. This is the combined consequence of Propositions 4.1 and 5.1, not a verbatim separate proposition in the manuscript. Its proof must construct the word-RAM program and establish correctness and all costs using the inherited algorithms and reductions. No inner-algorithm oracle or correctness assumption is supplied as a hypothesis. The uniform word-width requirement in the shared specification is part of the formalization obligation.

items.theorem_title: Deterministic integer 3SUM in O(n^1.999017) word-RAM steps
items.natural_language_statement:
For each fixed $\kappa\in\mathbb N$, there exist a finite deterministic word-RAM program $P$, a natural number $b$, and a step bound $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. For every $n$, input $x:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb Z$ with $|x_i|\le n^\kappa$, and every $W\ge b(\operatorname{Nat.log2}(n)+1)$, the program halts within $T(n)$ steps and accepts exactly when three pairwise distinct indices have sum zero. Equal values at distinct indices are allowed; no witness is required; inputs of size less than three are rejected.

The exact time requirement is $\exists K\in\mathbb N\;\forall n\ge2,\ T(n)^{1000000}\le K n^{1999017}$, equivalent to $T(n)=O(n^{1.999017})$. The target instantiates the campaign template without changing its definitions.

Source: Theorem 1.1 of Xu's sharp-tail manuscript. The manuscript states $\kappa\ge1$ and a sufficiently large logarithmic word width; the campaign additionally makes uniformity over all larger widths explicit. The case $\kappa=0$ follows from the $\kappa=1$ bound for $n\ge1$, with $n=0$ handled separately. The formal development must justify this interface adaptation. The improved bound is a proposed formalization target, not an already Lean-certified result.
